title: The Rhythm Club corner: Jelly Roll Morton and Chick Webb
summary: As a student he passed the Rhythm Club, remembering Jelly Roll saying he taught everyone to swing.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Okay. I used to go to the Lafayette theater, then the Rhythm Club used to be right in there. I used to come right past the Rhythm Club.
Yeah.
Alright. Let's go back. We were just doing something good there. We said -- we'd gone back to the Lafayette.
Mm hmm.
We said the Rhythm Club, and I said who was standing on the corner.
(laugh) Well, I remember there was always Begangles around.
Mm hmm.

And, I remember once -- that's when the Rhythm Club had moved -- from one block to the next block. The same direct location, but on the next side -- which is funny, you know, that they would put it in the same spot. Used to be 131st St. -- right close to the stage entrance -- to go backstage, see.
Yeah.
And, then they moved it on the next street, which is 132nd St.
Yeah.
--The identical spot -- just -- but -- opposite on the next street. And one day I -- naturally when I'd come through there I would always, you know, go by there --
Yeah.
-- you know. See who I could see.
Have a look-see. Yeah.
Yeah. People. Peep in.
Yeah.
And, so --Jelly Roll was out there one day --
Oh?
And, he was saying clearly "I taught all you So and So's how to swing".
(laugh)
And, I said --. I don't -- you know. I don't remember whether I liked that or not. But, I -- you know -- it's Jelly Roll, you know. [Who] could afford to say -- (laugh).
Who's going to argue?
Oh Chick Webb
I was just going to say -- did you ever see Chick on the corner
I might have. I don't remember.
I mean, because he used to --
I'm sure -- I'm sure I --
look inside the crowd and he was in the middle.
Yes. I'm sure I've seen him, you know, -- I had to.
Well, Freddie, alright. You were taking yourself back there.
Yes. Okay. That's -- that's before I had to go back home to bury my mother.
Yeah. Yeah.
